title: Spot
description: One physical viewpoint in Seoul with one or more historical photographs aligned to it. Platform-neutral: no pixel or CSS values, only geographic, angular and normalized (0..1) quantities.

id.description: Stable slug. Never renamed once published; it is the share URL.

status.description: draft = data being filled in; surveyed = viewpoint verified on site; published = visible in the app.

viewpoint.description: Where the user must stand and which way to look for the primary historical photo to align.

heading_deg.description: Compass bearing of the camera's optical axis, degrees clockwise from TRUE north. Magnetic declination is applied by the app, never baked in here.

hfov_deg.description: Horizontal field of view of the historical photo as estimated from its content. Drives how much of the live camera frame the overlay should cover.

confidence.description: rough = guessed from the map; estimated = derived from landmarks in the photo; surveyed = verified on site with a phone.

notes.description: How the position and heading were derived. Free text, Korean.

guide.description: What the app shows to get the user into position before the camera opens.

stand_here_image.description: Relative path under /spots/<id>/ to a present-day photo of the exact standing position.

landmarks.description: Things still standing today that the user can use to confirm the heading. Order = importance.

present.description: A pre-shot present-day photo from the viewpoint, for remote mode (users not on site). Optional until published.

historical.description: Historical photographs for this viewpoint, oldest first. The first entry is the primary alignment target; later entries appear on the period selector.

id.description: Slug local to this spot, e.g. 1964-opening.

year.description: null when the archive gives no date at all.

date.description: Full date when the archive provides one (Seoul Metropolitan Archives usually does).

media_type.description: Hand-tinted postcards are common in the 1910s-30s material; the UI labels them so users do not mistake tinting for colour photography.

description.description: The archive's own caption, verbatim. Often the best clue for camera position.

view.description: Where this photo sits in the world, when it differs from the spot's viewpoint. Lets several photos from the same standpoint face different directions (a partial panorama). Missing fields fall back to viewpoint.

file.description: Base filename under /spots/<id>/. The image pipeline derives sizes from it; do not put a size suffix here.

projection.description: flat = an ordinary photograph placed at view.heading_deg with view.hfov_deg. equirect = a full 360x180 panorama (2:1); its centre column faces view.heading_deg and hfov is implied.

original_ref.description: Where the master came from (archive URL or download endpoint). Master itself lives in /archive-raw/ and is not committed.

crop.description: Normalized (0..1) sub-rectangle of the master used for alignment, to remove frames, captions or postcard borders. null = whole image.

archive_id.description: The archive's own identifier, e.g. H-TRNS-103296-809 or RG5-SR79-IT329.

url.description: Detail page. Must stay reachable; it is shown to users as the original link.

producer.description: As stated by the archive, e.g. 서울특별시 공보실.

type.description: Only licenses that allow commercial use AND derivatives are listed. If a photo is KOGL-2/3/4 it does not enter this file.

evidence.description: badge = KOGL mark on the record page; metadata = record says 이용유형 제한없음 etc.; statement = institutional statement covering the collection (weaker; requires evidence_url).

evidence_quote.description: Verbatim sentence proving the license, captured at collection time.

attribution.description: Exact attribution string the app must display.

alignment.description: Hints that help the user (and later, code) line the photo up. All positions normalized 0..1 within the cropped image.
